findings.title: TOCTOU: symlink swap between pathScope check and mkdir/write wins race
findings.why_it_matters: resolveWithinBase/resolveRelativeWithinBase return the ORIGINAL lexical path (not the resolved realpath) after doing a point-in-time realpath check. Callers then do async fs work against that lexical path with multiple await gaps before the operation that matters. Concretely, PUT /api/fs/file (filesystem.ts) does: resolveWithinBase(check) -> await stat() [conflict check] -> await atomicWrite() [mkdir(recursive) -> writeFile(tmp) -> rename]. If the 'nearest existing ancestor' walk-up in realpathNearest validated a NOT-YET-EXISTING path component (e.g. session/newdir/newfile.txt where newdir doesn't exist yet), an attacker with write access to the session folder (e.g. the agent process itself, or a second concurrent API caller) can create `newdir` as a symlink to an arbitrary directory (e.g. the user's home dir) in the window between the check and atomicWrite's mkdir call. Node's `mkdir(dirname, {recursive:true})` and `writeFile`/`rename` all follow symlinks for intermediate path components, so the temp file and final rename land inside the symlink target, fully outside the session sandbox -- defeating the realpath hardening this PR just added. The race window is widened by the two intervening `await stat()` calls, and an attacker can retry the symlink-swap in a tight loop to win probabilistically.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve once and operate on file descriptors/realpaths from then on: open the target with O_NOFOLLOW (or fs.realpathSync right before the syscall that matters, e.g. immediately before atomicWrite's rename) and re-verify containment on the descriptor's realpath, not the lexical path. At minimum, re-run resolveWithinBase (or a fresh realpath containment check) immediately before atomicWrite in filesystem.ts's PUT /file handler to shrink the window, and document the residual risk in pathScope.ts's docstring rather than implying the re-check is race-free.
evidence: pathScope.ts:64-70 resolveWithinBase does a point-in-time realpath check via realpathContained() but returns `resolved` (the pre-check lexical path), not the checked realpath.

pathScope.ts realpathNearest() explicitly permits not-yet-existing path segments by walking up to the nearest existing ancestor and re-attaching trailing (non-existent) segments -- this is the documented 'creating a new file' allowance.

filesystem.ts:158-187 PUT /file: `const resolved = resolveWithinBase(...)` at line 158, then `await stat(resolved)` (conflict check, line 174), then `await atomicWrite(resolved, content)` (line 186) -- two await points between check and use.

atomicWrite.ts: `await mkdir(path.dirname(filePath), {recursive:true})` then `writeFile(tmpPath,...)` then `rename(tmpPath, filePath)` -- all three follow symlinks for intermediate directory components, so a symlink planted at `dirname(filePath)` after the pathScope check but before this call redirects the entire write.

pathScope.test.ts's new symlink tests (all added in this diff) only assert the point-in-time check rejects an already-existing escaping symlink; none simulate a symlink created/swapped between check and use, so the TOCTOU gap is untested.

findings.title: Synchronous tmux kill-server can block Electron main thread for 3s at quit
findings.why_it_matters: killTmuxServerBestEffort() is invoked synchronously inside the 10s shutdown-timeout callback for 'Quit & Stop All' users, and it calls execFileSync (both for `which tmux` with no timeout, and for `tmux -L <socket> kill-server` with a 3s timeout). execFileSync blocks the entire Node/Electron main-process event loop -- the same thread that services window messages, the tray, and the run loop. Because the timeout callback runs entirely synchronously before calling resolve() (which lets Promise.race proceed to app.quit()), a stuck graceful shutdown now takes 10s + up to 3s (+ unbounded time for the untimed `which` call) of the main process being completely unresponsive, right at the moment a user is already waiting on a slow quit. On macOS this is exactly the kind of main-thread stall that can trigger the OS's 'Application Not Responding' force-quit path, which would kill Argus before its own graceful cleanup (e.g. saveWindowState, the very kill-server call in flight) completes -- ironically defeating the escalation's own goal of leaving no orphaned processes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the async `execFile` (already imported for other calls) instead of execFileSync for both the `which tmux` lookup and the kill-server call, awaiting them with an explicit timeout via Promise.race/AbortController so the main-process event loop stays responsive while the escalation runs.
evidence: electron/src/main.ts:751-763 resolveTmuxBinary() calls `execFileSync('which', ['tmux'], {encoding:'utf-8'})` with no timeout option.

electron/src/main.ts:~810-820 the setTimeout callback for the 10s shutdown timeout calls `if (wantStopAll) killTmuxServerBestEffort();` synchronously BEFORE calling `resolve()`, so Promise.race (and therefore app.quit()) is gated on this blocking call completing.
testing.json (sibling reviewer) independently flags this path as 'completely untested', corroborating that this behavior has no test coverage to catch a regression here.

findings.title: Replay-snapshot cache not invalidated on session restart serves stale frame
findings.why_it_matters: getReplaySnapshot() now serves a cached tmux capture-pane frame for up to 250ms (REPLAY_SNAPSHOT_TTL_MS) to absorb reconnect storms. The cache is invalidated on destroySession (line 357) but NOT on restartSession (line 367). If a client captures/caches a snapshot for session X just before a restart, and a second client (mobile companion, second desktop window, or the same client rejoining) requests the replay within the remaining TTL window, it receives the PRE-RESTART terminal content instead of the freshly-spawned pty's state. This is most likely to actually occur precisely because 'restart' is often followed immediately by a rejoin from the same or another connected surface -- the same reconnect-storm pattern this cache was built to optimize for.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `this.replaySnapshotCache.delete(id)` at the start of restartSession(), mirroring the invalidation already done in the destroy path.
evidence: SessionManager.ts:90 declares `replaySnapshotCache`; line 357 deletes the cache entry inside the destroy path (`this.replaySnapshotCache.delete(id);`).
SessionManager.ts:367 `async restartSession(id)` has no corresponding `replaySnapshotCache.delete(id)` call.

SessionManager.ts:555-564 getReplaySnapshot() returns the cached frame verbatim whenever `Date.now() - cached.capturedAt < REPLAY_SNAPSHOT_TTL_MS`, with no session-generation/version check tying the cached frame to the current pty instance.

residual_risks: pathScope's realpath re-check is a point-in-time defense, not an atomicity guarantee; any consumer that does async work between the check and the actual filesystem syscall retains a TOCTOU window (the PUT /file route is the highest-value target since it's a controlled write; GET routes in filesystem.ts/symbols.ts have the same gap but lower impact since they're read-only or ripgrep-mediated).

The 'Quit & Stop All' shutdown path now has three sequential blocking/timeout stages (10s graceful timeout, then up to 3s tmux kill-server, then an untimed `which tmux` lookup on cold cache) that all run on the Electron main thread; under repeated slow-quit conditions (e.g. tmux itself wedged) this could compound into a multi-second main-thread freeze during every quit, not just the escalation case.

NgrokService's pendingStartReject double-settle guard (stop() vs. the process 'exit' handler) was verified correct by tracing both call sites and is well covered by NgrokService.test.ts's new tests -- no residual risk found there despite it being flagged as a specific area to probe.

asyncHandler wrapping across sessions.ts/git.ts/config.ts was checked line-by-line for the 'missing early return' hazard the task called out; every handler already returns immediately after each res.status()/res.json() call, so no double-send or contract-divergence issue was found in this batch.

Electron fuse-flip ordering (afterPack.cjs) was verified to run flipFuses() unconditionally before both the ad-hoc re-sign branch and the CSC_LINK early-return, so CI (signed) and local dev (ad-hoc) builds get identical fuse hardening -- no divergence found.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the pathScope TOCTOU window itself (symlink created/swapped concurrently with, or immediately after, a passing check) -- only point-in-time symlink rejection is covered.
No test covers getReplaySnapshot()'s cache TTL interacting with restartSession() (i.e. asserting a post-restart join does NOT receive a pre-restart cached frame).

No integration test simulates the Electron 'Quit & Stop All' path timing out and exercising killTmuxServerBestEffort() under a slow/hung tmux binary, to confirm the main process remains responsive or that the escalation itself doesn't get killed mid-execution.
